text:
ava: FYI I hit a weird thing running the Android sample behind a flaky LTE link: events sometimes get merged (e.g. two "events" arrive as one data block) and the Java SDK emits a single combined payload.
ryan: merged how? like chunk boundary got lost and we see `data: {..}\ndata: {..}` in one event?
ava: exactly. server sends two events with blank line between, but the client read returns a single buffer containing both and our parser treats any double-data lines as one event body. logs: `sse: accumulated buffer -> parsing event, data contains multiple JSONs, emitting single event`.
nate: hmm Java's parser concatenates consecutive data lines into a single event per SSE spec. But if the server sends two events separated by exactly one blank line, that should be two events. Are blank lines normalized?
ava: server is correct. Repro: run this tiny curl server loop:```
while true; do echo -e "event: update\ndata: {\"i\":1}\n\n"; sleep 0.2; echo -e "event: update\ndata: {\"i\":2}\n\n"; done | nc -l 8080;```
ava: on bad network we sometimes see the two `\n\n` collapsed at TCP layer so recv returns `...}\n\nevent: update\ndata: {\"i\":2}` in one read and our state machine doesn't insert the delimiter correctly.
ryan: sounds like reassembly bug: parser expects a delimiter at buffer edges. We need to iterate lines not raw reads and respect empty-line boundaries even if split mid-marker.
nate: agreed. Also saw Python client had a complementary bug: when reconnecting and using Last-Event-ID, it would include the final token again if reconnect happened during the same event boundary. leads to duplicate application-side state.
ava: that caused our sample app's cursor to go backward once. // Repro on Android: switch networks with small ms gap, watch duplicate id.
ryan: quick fixes: 1) ensure the streaming parsers treat CRLF sequences consistently and never assume a single recv maps to one event; 2) normalize incoming buffer by splitting on CRLF pairs and processing lines iteratively; 3) when emitting events, trim leading/trailing whitespace but honor empty-line event separators.
nate: also add a small resume-id dedupe layer on client side: if new event.id == last_emitted_id then drop. Should be opt-in for strict spec mode.
ava: will send a micro patch for Android/Java parser. I'll add unit tests for: boundary-split `event:` token, collapsed `\n\r\n` sequences, and delayed small recv returning parts of `data:` line.
ryan: can we add a network fuzz harness in sample apps repo that randomly coalesces or splits reads? That'll catch regressions across SDKs.
ate: (typo: nate) yes; also add a CI job to run the fuzz once per PR for sdk-parity label.
deploy-bot: created issue INF-2050: "sse: client reassembly + resume dedupe across SDKs" assigned to ava, ryan. Patch branch: sdk-fix/sse-reassembly. PR: https://git.redwood/internal/pr/4987
docs-bot: noted: update sample-apps/streaming.md with a diagnostic section "How to repro split/merged events" and add ENV var SSE_RESUME_DEDUPE=true for debugging.
ava: tiny note for onboarding: mention mobile networks can coalesce TCP segments and to use the fuzz tool when testing. saved me 2 hours.
ryan: thanks, add a short blurb in devex/sdks.md under Streaming caveats. I'll link the PR when ready.
nate: once patches land we should backport to Private runtime SDKs and Dedicated client libs. low-risk but need careful tests.
ava: TL;DR: parser reassembly bug on reads crossing boundaries & duplicate resume id on reconnect. patch + tests + fuzzer in progress.
ryan: :shipit:
